detail.title: Obedience-Driven Failures in Autonomous Systems
detail.summary: Autonomous systems relying solely on rigid operator instructions face significant performance and safety risks when encountering non-stationary environments. Effective autonomous agents require self-healing mechanisms and the capacity for self-generated goals to circumvent the failures associated with strict adherence to incomplete or narrow human-provided objectives.
detail.reason: Synthesizing evidence regarding rigid vs. autonomous goal setting to address project-specific questions on obedience-driven failures.
